changes.after: A function is a set of instructions you can call with an input.

before: function(n) { ... } creates an R function with a parameter named n. Assigning it to double_score gives the function a usable name.
A parameter is a local name for a supplied input. double_score(4) calls the function with argument 4.
The last evaluated expression is returned when there is no explicit return. Here n * 2 supplies the result.
Creating the function does not run its body. The print call displays the result of one particular call.
Expected result: [1] 8. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A function is a set of instructions you can call with an input.
Here n is the local name for the number supplied to the call.
The last expression in this function gives back its result.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
double_score <- function(n) {
  n * 2
}
print(double_score(4))
```
The output is `[1] 8`. The call gives four to the function and prints its answer, eight.
Follow the same function with seven as its input.
